bundles.drop_zone: Z4 top of cut, 1.2 m behind

steps.what: BCLS sets control pins and the temporary benchmark; crew hammers hub BC1 to BC4 at the 4 marked corners.
steps.app: Scan the hub, rover reads E/N, app shows the miss in mm

steps.what: Set 8 offset batter boards (2 posts and a ledger each) on lines SL1 to SL4 and string them; corners checked against the BCLS stakes.
steps.gate: Layout phase gate: 10 mm h/v (best practice)
steps.app: Site tab string-line view; Level tab for ledger height

steps.what: Load the LandXML TIN and PNEZD into the machine; slope 1H:1V planning value shown as needs-sign-off; dig to the toe stakes TOE1 to TOE4.
steps.gate: Excavation gate: bottom +-50 mm, toe +-100 mm
steps.app: Cut sheet by stake: C 2.50 means 2.50 m of cut at BC1

steps.what: Place spoil outside the setback lath; keep 1.2 m back from top of cut; call BC One Call locates before digging.
steps.app: Log tab records the locate ticket and spoil check photo

steps.what: Footing grade stakes FT1 to FT4 set at footing underside; as-built points logged for the survey certificate.
steps.gate: As-built within tolerance, over-dig below footing filled with lean concrete (BCBC 9.12.2.1)
steps.app: As-built heat map and over-dig volume

benefits.value: 5.9 mm median, 14.1 mm p95 worst corner (200-trial Monte Carlo)
benefits.detail: Synthetic BCLS control with simulated RTK noise (h 6 mm, v 12 mm, one pin disturbed 55 mm; detected 200 of 200 times). Latest report run: layout gate max 5.4 mm, pass. Needs real control and a real receiver before it is a field claim.

benefits.value: 233.0 m3 planning, 248.2 m3 TIN cut, 310 m3 loose, 32 loads
benefits.detail: Auguston demo lot, 1 m lidar ground, 0.6 m working room, swell 1.25, 10 m3 trucks. Planning grade, not a survey.

benefits.value: 0.1 m over-dig on the 155 m2 pad is about 16 m3 extra spoil plus lean-mix backfill
benefits.detail: Simulated as-built: pad RMS 31 mm, 89% of pad points inside +-50 mm, batter 100% inside +-100 mm, footing over-dig 0.10 m3 to fill. The simulation is not a field result.

benefits.value: 2.0 h of cutting, labelling and hunting removed for 59 stakes
benefits.detail: Assumes 3.0 min to cut, point-label and find each stake on site versus 1.0 min to pick a labelled one. Replace with your own time study.

benefits.value: No one enters the cut to check depth by grade rod; spoil and locate gates in the schedule
benefits.detail: OHSR 20.81(1) bars a worker from approaching closer to a bank than its depth unless it is sloped, benched or supported. This demo cut is 2.78 m deep (20.78: QRP needed because a structure is adjacent and the cut crosses the lot line by 2.8 m2). Stakes outside the batter and GPS grade control reduce entries; they do not replace the QRP or shoring.

benefits.value: 2.1% cut waste vs 10% typical order allowance
benefits.detail: Acucut 1D nester on this trade's 59 sticks: 12 boards, 58.52 m stock for 57.3 m of parts (bundle-window constrained runs add about 0.5 points). Conventional allowance 5 to 15% (BuildingScience). Difference about 9 bf, CAD 6 at CAD 700/MBF (estimate).

cell_does: Cuts 38x38 hub and grade stakes (chisel-pointed) and 38x89 batter-board posts and ledgers to length from the stake-out list (26 points, 4 string lines).
Laser-burns the point ID, code and a QR that opens the point in the crew app (E, N, ground, cut to bottom, to footing top). The planned cut/fill is a PLAN value; the rover check is the truth.
Cuts and numbers the spoil-setback lath (OHSR 20.90, 1.2 m back from top of cut) at 3 m chainage around the top of cut.
Bundles the whole kit by stake-out phase: corners, offsets and batter boards, footing and toe, top of cut.
cell_cannot: Survey. A BCLS sets control and certifies; HASWORKS HOMES never determines boundaries.
Mark a cut/fill value permanently: grade changes as the dig proceeds, so the burned text says PLAN and the live value is read in the app.
Machine control itself: the LandXML TIN and PNEZD points load into Trimble, Leica or Topcon systems (not yet tested on a real machine).

addons.name: Thin-stock clamp insert for 1x lath
addons.why: Cell clamps 38 mm dimension stock; 1x lath (19 mm) needs an insert and a coupon test.

addons.name: Small-parts handler
addons.why: 300 mm hub stakes fall through the outfeed gantry grip; use the pick-to-light bin.

app: Scan: aim the phone camera at a stake, QR opens the point (E, N, ground, cut, offsets).
Site: terrain, batters and the string-line rectangle on the true topography; stake-out core logic (parser, gate, math) exists, the receiver UI is not built yet.
Bundles: the 4 stake bundles in the order the crew needs them; Log: hash-chained install/check record.
code: BC OHS Regulation Part 20 (20.78, 20.79, 20.81, 20.90); BCBC 9.12; BC Land Surveyors Act (BCLS keeps legal survey)
summary: Pre-cut, laser-marked hub stakes, batter boards, grade stakes and spoil-setback lath, each with a QR that resolves to its exact plan coordinate, beside the LandXML and PNEZD files for GPS machine control.
highlight: Stake kit for 26 points with a QR to each plan coordinate, layout 5.9 mm p50 (simulated), 233 m3 planning / 248 m3 TIN cut, 32 truck loads.
routing: Acucut routing: the cell's nester groups this trade's parts by section and stock length, cuts them in bundle order (last-installed at the bottom), laser-burns the label, QR and every mark listed, and drops each bundle in its zone so the crew picks in install order.
